newsitem.title: UK: Mideast/Japan clean tankers steady, others dull.
newsitem.headline: Mideast/Japan clean tankers steady, others dull.

text.p: Mideast/Japan and Western Hemisphere clean tanker rates were steady but most other sectors were lacklustre this week, brokers said on Friday.
Galbraith's Ltd said Mideast/Japan 50,000 tonne rates held steady at W200, "and there is little sign of this diminishing, vessels already having been fixed into mid-May at these levels."
The Caribs/upcoast clean market firmed on Friday with 30,000 tonne cargoes done at W280/285, five to 10 points up from Thursday.

One broker said around 15 cargoes had been fixed in the last couple of days and there were a few vessels which were still in the market. But he said that in about 10 days ships would be returning to the Caribbean, which would cause rates to fall again.

But brokers E.A. Gibson were more optimistic, saying: "Further improvements are anticipated especially if the enquiry to lift clean product from Venezuela or the U.S. Gulf to the Far East should materialise into firm business."
The inter-U.K./Cont market suffered badly with few fixtures reported.
Gibson said levels of W220 for inter-UKC 22,000 tonners had persuaded two vessels to leave the clean sector for fuel oil trade, even though that market too has not enjoyed an encouraging period.
Brokers said the clean Med market was hampered by refinery maintenance and good volumes recently fixed from Northwest Euope to the Mediterranean, India and the Far East.
There was also movement of product from the Med to the U.S., with 33,000 tonne unleaded gasoline cargoes fixed at W235.

Galbraith's said charterers had covered all their movements for Mideast/India cargoes for April delivery and rates were therefore likely to decline next week to below W190 for 30,000 tonnes to West Coast India.
Brokers said elderly tonnage had been especially badly hit on Mideast/India voyages.
